Both files pass the Strata audit with a score of 100 (no findings). Summary of what was built in `src/screens/Screen.tsx` (+ `Screen.module.css`):

- **List of 6 mock scheduled payments** (Card with an inset list), each showing payee (Avatar), amount (Amount), next date, repeat frequency, and status (Badge, paired with a text label, never colour alone).
- **Pause/Resume** — immediate toggle from a per-row action Menu, confirmed via a toast.
- **Edit** — opens a Dialog (payee, amount, date, frequency fields) pre-filled from the row; Save updates the mock state.
- **Cancel** — opens an `AlertDialog` (danger tone) warning it can't be restored; once cancelled, the row loses its action menu entirely (badge shows "Cancelled", no way to resume/edit/re-cancel).
- **Schedule a payment** — header button opens a Dialog with the same field set, appending a new active payment on submit.

All UI comes from `@strata/react`/`@strata/icons`, styled only with `var(--strata-*)` tokens and logical CSS properties, with accessible names on every icon-only control. I avoided the `DatePicker`/`@internationalized/date` component since that package isn't a declared dependency in this app (would fail to resolve under pnpm's strict linking), using labelled `TextField`s for dates instead.

I can't run the dev server in this environment, so I wasn't able to visually verify it in a browser — flagging that per the instructions rather than claiming it's been tested live.
